when: 2026-08-02, taken on origin/main before any edit of this branch; corrected 2026-08-03 after independent review
what: The size of the post-combat clinch, named as a quantity and taken on the seed matrix. Nobody had measured what the owner's sentence corresponds to, so this file defines the measurement first and reports it second.
theOwnersWords: Когда все сгрудились после боя — потом не могут некоторое время разойтись и блокируют друг друга.

whatChangedInVersion2.controlWindow: The control used to be the 60 ticks ending at the wave's arrival. On `prepared` that interval is the muster: its journal sets muster_lead_ticks to 60 on tick 880 and PrototypeWorld.IsMusterActive is true from arriveTick - 60, so the two coincided tick for tick and the 'peacetime' half of the comparison was the one moment of the party when every creature drops its work and walks into a Watch zone of ten tiles. It carried 532 of the 737 refused steps of the old control. The window is now pushed back by muster_lead_ticks: `baseline` sets no lead and does not move at all, `prepared` is compared against the quiet stretch ending where its muster begins. Over the matrix the answer reverses — 782 against 526 rather than 782 against 737, and 154 clinch ticks against 106 rather than 194.
whatChangedInVersion2.theBucketAYieldMayNotTouch: `byArrived` used to hold every refused step whose blocker had no destination it was walking to. That is wrong for a blocker with no destination at all: PrimaryDestination returns a GridPoint? over a readonly record struct, so for a creature with no job, no meal and no muster it is null and the last clause of CanYield, `PrimaryDestination(creature) != creature.Position`, lifts to true — such a creature may be told to step aside. Split: byArrived 290, byNoDestination 17, and the reach of a yield rises from 327 to 344.
whatChangedInVersion2.theComparison: A way round used to be counted over all 782 refused steps and a yield only over the ones with a body in the way. The 93 refused steps whose next tile is empty at the end of the tick belong to the arbitration, not to a body, so they are now excluded from both sides: 639 against 344.
whatChangedInVersion2.theHistogramOfStandingStill: Last decisions used to be counted over all 1989 creature-ticks standing still while the conclusion was drawn about the 1121 in CreatureMode.Waiting. Restricted to Waiting the picture changes: waiting_stock_sufficient 850, refused_zone_unreachable 232, waiting_blocked_by_other 18.
whatChangedInVersion2.howItWasFound: All four by independent review of pull request #198, by measurement rather than by reading. Version 1 of this file is in the history of the branch.

tree.note: The base commit is on `main` and survives squash; the branch head is not, so it is described in prose instead (Issue #106). No file of the simulation is changed by this branch — only the test project gained the harness below.

howItWasMeasured.harness: tests/DungeonFortress.Simulation.Tests/PrototypePostCombatDispersalTests.cs, added by this branch. It walks each party tick by tick with PrototypeWorld.Step() and reads PrototypeWorld.GetSnapshot() after every tick.
howItWasMeasured.refusedSteps: Read from the canonical event log by LastTick, the way PrototypeTrafficTests reads them. A repeated identical decision coalesces into one entry whose LastTick advances on every tick it repeats, so scanning for LastTick == acted sees it on each of those ticks. Positions, modes and LastMoveTick are read from the snapshot, which does not coalesce.

definitions.cohort: the creatures in CreatureMode.Fighting on the tick before the wave's EndTick — exactly the set ResolveWave turns back into Waiting on that tick
definitions.window: the 60 ticks after EndTick. Sixty because the dungeon is 28 tiles wide, a harvest is 12 ticks and a cook batch 24, and it is a sixth of T.wave_interval_ticks, so it never reaches the next fight
definitions.measuredWindow: a window with at least one tick in it. Three of the sixteen waves end on the same tick the party does; they are printed and left out of every aggregate
definitions.clinchTicks: ticks of the window on which at least two cohort members were refused a step (waiting_blocked_by_other). Two, because one creature waiting for one tile is ordinary traffic
definitions.maxBlockedTogether: the most cohort members refused a step on one tick of one window
definitions.blocked: cohort creature-ticks with a refused step inside the window
definitions.background: the same counts over the 60 ticks ending at `arriveTick - muster_lead_ticks`, for the same creatures. This is the control, and the subtraction is what keeps it out of the muster
definitions.dispersalDelay: per cohort member, ticks from EndTick to the first tick it stands somewhere else; 60 if it never does
definitions.standingStill: cohort creature-ticks that neither moved nor were refused a step
definitions.idleAndStill: standingStill restricted to CreatureMode.Waiting — standing with no work rather than standing to do work
definitions.shortDetour: refused steps where a route to the same destination existed within 4 extra steps once every other creature counted as a wall
definitions.detourWithABody: shortDetour restricted to the refused steps a body was actually standing in the way of. This is the side of the mechanism comparison that is comparable with the reach of a yield
definitions.longerWayRound: refused steps where that route was strictly longer than the blind one — a different route, not the same one re-derived
definitions.walledIn: refused steps where no such route existed at all
definitions.nextTileFree: refused steps where the tile the step was for was empty at the end of the tick — the step was refused by the arbitration, not by a body, and no yield of anybody's could have cleared it
definitions.byArrived: refused steps whose next tile was held by a creature standing on its own destination. CanYield refuses to order such a creature aside, so no yield can ever clear these
definitions.byNoDestination: next tile held by a creature with no destination at all. CanYield allows this one to step aside, because `null != position`
definitions.byUrgent: next tile held by a creature with a meal reserved or mustering — CanYield refuses these unless the block is a proven dependency cycle
definitions.byEligible: next tile held by a creature walking somewhere that CanYield would allow to step aside
definitions.yieldCouldClear: byEligible and byNoDestination, restricted to blockers with an empty tile beside them. The whole of what the yield arbitration could ever buy

byFixture.reading: The two halves of the matrix say the same thing with different force, and neither says the post-combat window is quieter than peacetime. `baseline` has no muster at all, so its control never moved; the old average of 1.06 was that 2.08 pulled down by a `prepared` control that was itself a jam.

whereItHappens.reading: (10,7) and (11,7) are the kitchen, (14,7) and (15,7) the larder — the two doorways of the room the raiders walk to. (24,12) and (22,12) are the corridor of the south-eastern chamber the gate opens onto.

whatAnExCombatantThatNeitherWalkedNorWas.caveat: LastDecision is the last decision this creature took, not a decision it took on this tick. For a creature that decided nothing here it is several ticks old. That is still the right thing to count — a creature that has stopped deciding is one whose last decision is still standing — but it reads the past.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: The ticks after a fight are measurably more blocked than the ticks before one, on both halves of the matrix.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: 782 refused steps against 526 in the control (1.49) and 154 clinch ticks against 106 (1.45), over 13 measured windows and 3780 cohort creature-ticks. By fixture: `baseline` 426 against 205 (2.08), `prepared` 356 against 321 (1.11); clinch ticks 74 against 62 and 80 against 44 (1.82).
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: The owner's playtest sentence is confirmed by measurement. Version 1 of this file said the opposite — 1.06 and 0.79 — and it said it because the `prepared` control was the muster.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: The size of it is a single window rather than an average.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: baseline/20260727 wave 1: 292 refused steps in 60 ticks by a cohort of nine — 54 % of that cohort's creature-ticks — against 81 in the control window of the same nine creatures, a ratio of 3.6. Six of the nine were refused a step on the same tick. clinchTicks 53 of 60.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: This is the party the owner would have been watching, and it is now consistent with the `baseline` average of 2.08 rather than standing against a matrix average that pointed the other way.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: The larger half of «не могут разойтись» is not blocking at all.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: 1989 of 3780 cohort creature-ticks (53 %) were spent neither moving nor being refused a step, and 1121 of them (30 % of the window) in CreatureMode.Waiting. Among those 1121 the commonest last decision is waiting_stock_sufficient, 850 times — there is no work to be had — and the second is refused_zone_unreachable, 232 times (20.7 %). On baseline/20260728 wave 1 seven of eight ex-combatants never left the tile the fight ended on in 60 ticks, with 0 refused steps in the whole window.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: Two different pictures produce one complaint. A group that stands because it is jammed and a group that stands because it has nowhere to be look the same from above, and the second is the bigger of the two. It is not one diagnosis either: a fifth of it is a zone the creature cannot reach rather than work that does not exist.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: Of the refused steps, almost all had a way round.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: 728 of 782 (93.1 %) had a route to the same destination within 4 extra steps once every other creature was treated as a wall, and on 516 of them (66 %) that route was strictly longer than the blind one. Only 24 (3.1 %) had no route at all.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: The creature is not walled in. PrototypeMap.NextStep is a BFS that does not see bodies, so it hands out a step that Move then refuses, and the tile to walk around by is standing empty.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: The yield arbitration cannot clear most of these even in principle, and the ceiling is 344 rather than the 327 first published.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: 290 refused steps (37 %) were blocked by a creature standing on its own destination, which CanYield refuses to order aside, and 54 more (7 %) by a creature with a meal reserved or mustering — 344 (44 %) out of reach of a yield by design. Of the 345 blocked by a creature a yield may move (328 walking somewhere, 17 with no destination at all), 344 had an empty tile beside them. On 680 of 782 ticks (87 %) no chosen_traffic_yield was planned anywhere in the world.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: A creature with no destination at all may be told to step aside — `PrimaryDestination` is null and the last clause of CanYield lifts to true — and version 1 of this file put 17 such refused steps on the wrong side. The correction moves the ceiling up, not down.
